30180101.text: We've finally made it to Caravan Ribat. It's pretty lively here!

30180102.text: So just past this wall is the desert, huh...

30180103.text: Oh wow, Paimon remembers hearing people call this the Wall of Samiel. It's made to block sandstorms from the outside... If it's this tall, it's gotta be the divine work of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, right?

30180302.text: Ugh, how did we lose 'em? They were just here a second ago...

30180303.text: More Eremite mercenaries? Who're they working for this time... Anyway, Traveler, it seems like we were being followed again!

30180304.text: You were too careless. You should have noticed those hopeless amateurs trailing you a long time ago.

30180307.text: There's no need to thank me. I've never cared to keep track of personal favors.

30180308.text: All I did was correct a mistake I happened to come across. It's a habit I developed at the Akademiya.

30180309.text: You really gave Paimon a scare, Alhaitham! We never thought we'd run into you here.

30180310.text: Last time we met at Port Ormos, didn't you say you were going back to the Akademiya? Wait... don't tell Paimon that you're here to take us back on their orders!

30180311.text: Oh, so you've already landed yourselves on the Akademiya's hit list? Haha, I can't say that I didn't expect it.

30180312.text: However, had I wished to turn you over to the Akademiya, don't you think you'd already be the Eremites' honored guests by now?

30180313.text: Oh, right... You do have a point.

30180314.text: Did you participate in the sages' big project?

30180316.text: I have no interest in running errands for that project. As a scholar, I've always belonged to the camp that promotes researcher autonomy.

30180317.text: And these days, you are more fascinating than anything the sages can offer.

30180318.text: So, you were actually looking for me?

30180319.text: Hmm, not quite. To tell you the truth... I'm still investigating the Divine Knowledge Capsule. Unfortunately, I've run into some difficulties.

30180320.text: Everyone says the capsule originated in the desert and was eventually moved to Port Ormos. If I am to get to the bottom of this, I must understand how the capsule first came to be.

30180321.text: Which brings me back to you, and why you're so interesting.

30180322.text: The leader of Ayn Al-Ahmar used the Divine Knowledge Capsule right in front of you, and upon seeing him, your expression became perplexed, and you were lost in thought for quite some time.

30180323.text: To have that kind of reaction, I think you must have realized something. Are you interested at all in sharing what you've been hiding from me?

30180315.text: (It must be because I was so shocked to hear those words again... "world... forget me...")

30180324.text: Alhaitham, you really have a ridiculous eye for detail! What kind of person even notices and remembers stuff like that...

30180401.text: Before us lies Aaru Village, the safe haven of the desert folk.

30180402.text: Whoa, this landscape is really something else. What a cool place! Let's go check it out!

30180403.text: Unless my memory fails me, we have barely spoken two words to each other before now at the Akademiya. Would you care to enlighten me as to when and how I invited the General Mahamatra's wrath?

30180404.text: Alhaitham, do not think you can escape my judgment just because you managed to escape my attack.

30180405.text: "Judgment"? So, that's how you'd characterize your actions here, is it? Or would "elimination" perhaps be a more accurate description?

30180406.text: Had I used my full strength, not even this traveler would have been able to stop me.

30180407.text: Though styled like an assassination, I sought only to ensure that my target would be unable to flee or resist. Standard practice for the matra, as well you know.

30180408.text: Seemed to me more like your own personal touch.

30180409.text: Uh, wh—who is that, Alhaitham? Did you call him "General Mahamatra"?

30180410.text: Yes... General Mahamatra Cyno, head of all the matra at the Akademiya. He's a formidable hunter, and the ultimate nightmare for any who have committed academic crimes.

30180411.text: You seem to have placed a lot of trust in Alhaitham, to the point of blocking an attack for him.

30180412.text: If I were you, I'd never choose to side with him. I wouldn't believe a single word that comes out of his mouth.

30180413.text: I have been pursuing this scribe for a long time. I urge you, stand back and do not seek to defend him any longer. Otherwise... there will be consequences.

30180416.text: Has Alhaitham done something wrong? Paimon doesn't think he's as bad as you've made him out to be.

30180417.text: I won't waste my breath explaining things. Alhaitham, I saw it during our fight...

30180418.text: Take it out. The Divine Knowledge Capsule you're hiding on your person. Unless you want me to retrieve it for myself?

30180420.text: Very perceptive of you... Nothing escapes a matra's senses.

30180421.text: Wait, the Divine Knowledge Capsule!? Didn't it fall into the matra's hands in Port Ormos?

30180422.text: So you did lie to us.

30180423.text: No wonder you speak with such confidence, Cyno. But I must admit, I am very curious... What does this capsule mean to you?

30180424.text: And why, as General Mahamatra of the Akademiya, are you all alone in the desert?

30180425.text: As far as I'm aware, the other matra have been speculating about your disappearance.

30180426.text: Have you been given a mission that's... let's say, morally dubious?

30180427.text: If I was the real target of your mission, what was stopping you from simply using your authority and resources to judge me within the walls of the Akademiya?

30180428.text: Is it a mission from the sages?

30180453.text: I should have known you'd be difficult to deal with.

30180430.text: #You two... Ugh, what should we do, {NICKNAME}? Paimon feels like we can't trust either of them...

30180431.text: Ahem... Well look at you two, acting all tough and self-righteous over there.

30180433.text: #Great, {NICKNAME}, finally someone that we can trust!

30180434.text: You gotta help us out here! Otherwise, these two are gonna start fighting again...

30180435.text: Yeah, sure looks that way... Two giants from the Akademiya, duking it out once and for all. Not something you get to see every day, that's for sure.

30180436.text: Listen, I know you academic types love to fill up your big brains with self-righteous morality, and lord your empty rules and virtues over each other...

30180437.text: But how dare you bring your petty disputes into the safe haven of Aaru Village?

30180438.text: It seems like someone's gonna have to beat some sense into your thick skulls until you finally learn to respect these grounds!

30180506.text: "Hey, wanna play sardines with three people who wanna tear each other limb from limb?" "Sure, why not, sounds fun!"...

30180507.text: Ah... The air's so thick and heavy, Paimon can hardly keep floating anymore...

30180508.text: My sincerest apologies, everyone. This is the home of our village chief. I will have to ask you to make do with this small room until the sandstorm dies down.

30180509.text: Please let me introduce myself. I am Candace, protector of Aaru Village.

30180510.text: Ah, our savior has come at last!

30180511.text: Nice to meet you, Candace! The name's Paimon! Thank you so much for helping us!

30180513.text: Hehe, there's no need to thank me. It's only right to help each other when the weather gets rough.

30180514.text: Wow... She's so gentle and caring, like a nice older sister! ...Unlike those guys over there.

30180515.text: Alright, now that we're all better acquainted, we should return to the topic at hand.

30180516.text: As a guardian charged with the responsibility to protect my fellow villagers from harm, I was observing your conflict from afar, even before the sandstorm started.

30180517.text: And now that you have set foot within Aaru Village itself, it is all the more my responsibility to make absolutely sure that you pose no threat whatsoever to us.

30180518.text: So please, have an honest and sincere conversation with one another, and put your hostile feelings to rest.

30180519.text: If anyone dares to start anything again while they are under this roof... I will not hesitate to send them out for some quality time with the creatures of the sandstorm.

30180520.text: Oh, uh... On second thought, Paimon may have misjudged Candace's character.

30180522.text: And that goes for you too, Miss Dehya.

30180525.text: Hehe, that's what I like to hear. So, which of you will begin?

30180526.text: I was supposed to be a mediator, but uh... I might've gotten a little too involved just now. Anyway, one of those two should probably start talking.

30180527.text: Wait, that was you trying to be a mediator?

30180529.text: I have nothing to hide, so there is no shame in explaining myself.

30180530.text: While Alhaitham wasn't wrong about the other matra not knowing my whereabouts, it's not because I've been assigned a morally dubious mission.

30180531.text: Rather... I've chosen to exile myself.

30180533.text: A little while ago, I discovered that there was data missing in the Akademiya's project planning and development files. What little they did report clearly did not match the project's actual progress.

30180534.text: As General Mahamatra, I had the responsibility and authority to request an audit. However, to my surprise, the person responsible for the erroneous data was none other than Grand Sage Azar himself.

30180535.text: I tried to investigate the issue myself before submitting a formal audit request, but I soon found that all leads and potential pieces of incriminating evidence were carefully concealed from me.

30180536.text: I began to realize that... they were cautious of me from the very beginning.

30180537.text: Unsurprisingly, the Grand Sage rejected my audit request as soon as the submission reached his desk. He even said to me:

30180538.text: "The power of the General Mahamatra is granted by the sages. You have no right to judge us."

30180539.text: So they really are up to no good.

30180540.text: I realized then that to the Grand Sage, the matra are nothing more than tools for the sages to assert and maintain their control over knowledge.

30180541.text: The vows that we took, the principles that we strive to uphold... They are meaningless to the Akademiya of today.

30180542.text: So you then decided to exile yourself?

30180543.text: I believed it would be wise to flee the Akademiya before the sages had a chance to take action against me. This way, they can no longer see nor predict my actions.

30180544.text: I will never give up on this investigation... There's no need for someone else to give me power or authority. Once I find the truth, I will administer judgment by my own name.

30180545.text: Cyno seems to have the same goal as us... We're all investigating the sages!

30180546.text: Plus, now that he's no longer the General Mahamatra, he somehow feels a lot less scary!

30180549.text: Well, Cyno, if that's your story, then why did you see Alhaitham as a target?

30180550.text: When I was investigating the matter in the Akademiya, I overheard a conversation between Alhaitham and a sage.

30180551.text: #The sages asked you to investigate a {M#blond}{F#blonde}-haired Traveler. Do you dispute this, Alhaitham?

30180553.text: Like many parts of the project, this assignment was undocumented. Now, throw in your suspicious behavior with the Divine Knowledge Capsule, and I think we deserve an explanation.

subQuests.subQuestName: Check the situation outside the village chief's house

30180601.text: Whoa... Candace, you're still fighting? You've been out here dealing with these creatures the entire time?

30180602.text: Yes, they just keep coming in waves... I've lost count of how many I've defeated. Before I realized it, even the sandstorm had stopped...

30180606.text: Leave this round to us! I got interrupted earlier, but now I have something to take my anger out on!

30180607.text: Hehe, it's been a while since I've seen the Flame-Mane in action. I'll leave these to you then.

30180608.text: #I'll be sure to put on a good show! {NICKNAME}, let's go!

30180801.text: The creatures stopped appearing. Was that the last of them?

30180802.text: What we fought just now was probably the aftermath of the sandstorm, so we should be safe for the time being.

30180803.text: Well fought, everyone. No injuries, I hope?

30180805.text: Ah, my apologies, I haven't had a chance to greet you yet. I had my hands full taking care of the village's elderly and children.

30180806.text: I am the chief of Aaru Village. Everyone usually calls me Uncle Anpu.

30180809.text: Sir, I am also originally from the desert, but I have not been back for some time now. May I ask if such sandstorms are common?

30180810.text: I can't say they've always been common, but recently, the storms have become increasingly severe and frequent.

30180811.text: Besides sandstorms, we also occasionally get earthquakes... According to an investigator who stayed in the village a while ago, these unusual natural phenomena are related to the withering of Irminsul.

30180812.text: Hmm, another effect of Irminsul's withering...

30180813.text: So... Irminsul's withering causes Withering Zones in the forest, and sandstorms and earthquakes here in the desert?

30180814.text: Everything in the natural world is inextricably connected to Irminsul. These "regional symptoms" can indeed be a reflection of Irminsul's present state.

30180815.text: *sigh* Everyone in Aaru Village needs to take good care of themselves.

30180816.text: Uh, speaking of which, why haven't I seen a single Village Keeper since I got here?

30180817.text: Village Keeper? Who are they? Village guards like Candace?

30180818.text: Does your curiosity know no bounds... "Village Keeper" is how Aaru Village refers to mad scholars exiled here by the Akademiya.

30180819.text: Most of them are scholars who lost their sanity after a period of training in the Avidya Forest.

30180820.text: The Akademiya believes that their crazed mutterings may have a negative effect on the psyches of other scholars, so they're forcibly exiled to the desert... Though if you ask me, it's all a boatload of nonsense.

subQuests.subQuestName: Exchange information with Cyno somewhere else

30180901.text: Although I've sent myself into exile, I'm still doing essentially the same things as before...

30180902.text: Do you still have any questions for me before we start our investigation?

30180903.text: Why do they refer to the mad scholars as Village Keepers?

30180904.text: One of my former subordinates told me that this title has its origins in a strange incident.

30180905.text: The Akademiya has long exiled mad scholars to Aaru Village. A mysterious phenomenon exists here...

30180906.text: When mad scholars first arrive, they are as incoherent and deranged as before. But after spending some time here, they invariably begin to calm down.

30180907.text: Initially, the people of Aaru Village greatly resented having to take in the mad scholars. But a strange incident one night changed that...

30180908.text: Aaru Village was struck by the strongest earthquake in living memory. Seeing buildings on the verge of collapse all around him, the then chief of the village was preparing to take everyone to safety...

30180909.text: Suddenly, he noticed a mad scholar crouching in a corner, caressing the ground with his hands. A soft, green light radiated from him, like a divine glow against the backdrop of night.

30180910.text: Despite the powerful tremors that ripped through the ground that night, all the houses remained upright, almost as if they had grown roots reaching deep into the ground. In the end, not a single building collapsed, and no one was hurt.

30180911.text: After that, the people of Aaru Village treated the mad scholars with greater kindness, and began to refer to them as the Village Keepers.

30180912.text: #A soft, green light... A mad scholar protecting Aaru Village... Hmm, what do you make of it, {NICKNAME}?

30180915.text: Paimon thinks so, too! Actually, Cyno, do you know if any of the mad scholars continued to wear their Akasha Terminals at Aaru Village?

30180916.text: In theory, they would continue wearing them so the Akademiya could still monitor their activities. With that said, the main Akasha system would no longer have any interaction with them.

30180917.text: Oh, no wonder! Everything makes sense, then! Add in the fact that they calmed down... It was probably Nahida who calmed them...

30180918.text: ...If you are able to draw a conclusion from this one story alone, then it appears you possess much more information than I do.

30180919.text: So, what do you make of the story?

30180956.text: As you approach the village chief's house, Cyno asks Isak to wait nearby.

30180957.text: Cyno is super vigilant... Is this what all the matra are like?

30180959.text: We just wanted to confirm something with you. Do you know a boy by the name of Isak?

30180960.text: Hehe, I had a feeling he'd go looking for you.

30180961.text: Huh? You knew this would happen?

30180962.text: Yes. Although he tried his best to stay hidden, I still noticed him eavesdropping outside the window. He really wants to get his grandfather back.

30180963.text: Isak's parents were both Eremite mercenaries who rarely returned to the village after finding employment in the city. He was raised by his grandfather.

30180964.text: Unfortunately, it was only a few years before his grandpa passed away. Isak was still very young at the time, so various families in the village took turns caring for him so he could survive.

30180965.text: Later, an elderly mad scholar arrived in the village. Isak thought the scholar bore a striking resemblance to his grandfather, and thus often spied on the man.

30180966.text: However, the scholar was unkempt in appearance and incoherent in speech. Although Isak referred to the man as his "grandpa," he was afraid and didn't dare to approach him.

30180967.text: One summer night, the oft-mumbling and bumbling "grandpa" suddenly calmed down and seemed to become more lucid. He even noticed Isak hiding in the distance.

30180968.text: So "Grandpa" walked up to Isak and patted him on the head. He even took Isak to the entrance of the village, where he patiently taught the boy the names of the stars, and accompanied Isak until he fell asleep.

30180969.text: The next morning, Isak woke up and wanted to go find his "grandpa" again, only to realize his grandpa no longer recognized him. However, even so, Grandpa retained his calm expression.

30180970.text: It's said that those who saw the scholar claimed he no longer appeared to be crazy, but appeared to be living in his own world, almost as if he were sleepwalking.

30180971.text: Isak was thrilled that his "grandpa" was able to find peace, and would follow him all the time asking him things like, "Grandpa, want me to take you somewhere fun?" or "Grandpa, could you tell me stories about the stars again?"

30180972.text: All this somehow just makes Paimon feel really sad... It seems like they both deserve so much better...

30180973.text: Perhaps. Nearly everyone who lives in the desert has some form of hardship or regret. But even so, we must still continue on with our lives.

30180974.text: It's also my reason for fighting. I must continue to protect this land.

30180975.text: ("Lucid grandpa" was probably Nahida... She must have soothed the other mad scholars as well.)

30180977.text: (From the look on Cyno's face, he's probably connected the dots as well.)

30180978.text: Maybe the people have always had a considerate god watching over them.

30180979.text: Huh? What did you say, Cyno?

30180980.text: No, nothing. As long as Isak keeps his word and doesn't get in our way, we can take him along.

30180981.text: Perhaps you are more compassionate than I gave you credit for. Please accept my thanks on Isak's behalf, Cyno.

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the village chief's house

30180984.text: We've cleared everything up! Let's go find your grandpa!

30180985.text: Really!? Wow, thank you so much!

30180986.text: Your grandpa will be found safe and sound.

30180988.text: Alright, let's ask the local residents some questions first.

30189901.text: Alhaitham went that way — let's hurry up and follow him. Wonder what he's up to...
